skill.name: generating-rbs-inline
skill.description: Generates RBS-inline type annotations as comments in Ruby source files and guides validation with rbs-inline, RBS, and Steep.
skill.summary: Add precise RBS-inline type comments to Ruby source files and validate the generated signatures.
skill.author: DmitryPogrebnoy

security_audit.summary: All static detections were adjudicated as false positives from Markdown code spans, RBS annotation syntax, documentation links, and reference example code. No evidence found for prompt injection, credential exposure, unauthorized network access, or malicious execution intent.

- You MUST NOT use `untyped`. Infer the proper type instead.
- You MUST prepend any command with `bundle exec` if the project has Gemfile.
- You MUST use `# @rbs` comment syntax for inline annotations.
- You MUST NOT use regular RBS signatures and `.rbs` files in the project.
- Pay extra attention to `Data` and `Struct` types
- Review all annotations and replace `untyped` with proper types.
- Use `untyped` only as a last resort when type cannot be determined.
Perform this step ONLY if the project Gemfile includes `steep` gem AND the project has Steepfile.

content.user_title: Generate Inline RBS Types for Ruby
content.value_statement: Ruby teams need type signatures close to source code. This skill adds RBS-inline comments and guides validation without creating separate RBS files.
actual_capabilities: Adds the rbs_inline magic comment to Ruby source files.
Creates inline method, attribute, constant, and variable type comments.
Handles Data.define and Struct.new annotation patterns.
Replaces untyped annotations with inferred concrete types when possible.
Guides validation with rbs-inline, RBS validate, and Steep when configured.
Uses syntax references and Zeitwerk examples for annotation style.
limitations: Does not run project Ruby code and should not execute application behavior.
Needs enough source context to infer precise types safely.
Metaprogramming and dynamic dispatch may require user clarification.
Requires local RBS tools to validate generated signatures.

use_cases.title: Annotate Application Code
use_cases.description: Add inline type comments to service objects, models, and plain Ruby classes during normal feature work.

use_cases.title: Document Gem APIs
use_cases.description: Place type information next to public methods so maintainers can review API contracts in source files.

use_cases.title: Migrate Toward Static Typing
use_cases.description: Introduce RBS-inline gradually while avoiding broad untyped annotations and validating generated signatures.

prompt_templates.title: Annotate a Simple File
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one Ruby file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use generating-rbs-inline to add RBS-inline annotations to this Ruby file. Avoid untyped and ask before guessing unclear types.

prompt_templates.title: Add Missing Method Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for an existing class.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Ruby class and add inline RBS comments for public and private methods using callers and tests for context.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Data and Struct Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Annotate these Data.define and Struct.new declarations with RBS-inline comments, including attributes and constructor behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Typed Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with local validation tools.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate precise inline annotations for this module, run available RBS validation steps, and refine any reported type errors.

output_examples.input: A Ruby user class has an initializer, readers, and a greeting method.
output_examples.output: The skill adds inline annotations for attributes, constructor parameters, and return values, then flags any uncertain inferred type.

output_examples.input: A Struct declaration stores account objects and supports keyword initialization.
output_examples.output: The skill adds attribute types, describes constructor forms, and notes how keyword initialization changes accepted arguments.

output_examples.input: A project already has Steep configured with generated RBS files.
output_examples.output: The skill generates inline comments, validates produced signatures when tools are available, and reports type errors for review.

best_practices: Review constructors, attribute readers, and visibility before adding annotations.
Prefer precise unions, nilable types, and generics instead of untyped.
Generate RBS output and validate it before considering annotations complete.
anti_patterns: Adding broad untyped annotations to silence unknown behavior.
Editing Steepfile to hide type errors from incorrect annotations.
Running arbitrary project code when only type comments are needed.

faq.question: Does this skill create separate RBS files?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on RBS-inline comments inside Ruby source files. Generated RBS files are only used for validation.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Will it use untyped for hard cases?
faq.answer: It should avoid untyped. When a type is unclear, it should ask for more context or explain the uncertainty.

faq.question: Does it run Ruby application code?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly says not to run project Ruby code while adding annotations.

faq.question: How does validation work?
faq.answer: It can generate RBS output, run RBS validation, and use Steep only when the project is configured for it.

faq.question: What Ruby patterns need extra care?
faq.answer: Data.define, Struct.new, metaprogramming, dynamic dispatch, and callback-heavy code need careful review before annotation.
